name: @unblockingapi/mcp

tools.name: unblock_fetch
tools.description: Fetch any URL through UnblockingAPI, bypassing bot detection, CAPTCHAs and geo-blocks with rotating residential proxies. Returns clean HTML (scripts, styles and SVGs already stripped). Start with render=false; set render=true only when the response is missing content because the page needs JavaScript. Pass a template name to get structured JSON instead of HTML (see list_templates). Costs 1 credit per successful fetch; failures are free.

url.description: The HTTP/HTTPS URL to fetch. Media and binary files are rejected.

render.description: Render with a real browser (executes JavaScript). Needed for SPAs and lazy-loaded content. Slower (up to ~2 min worst case). Default false.

location.description: 2-letter country code to proxy through (e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'de', 'se'). Any ISO country.

wait_for.description: Render-only. When to capture: 'stable' (default — once the DOM stops changing), 'domcontentloaded' (immediately), 'networkidle', or any CSS selector (wait until it is visible, then settle). Prefer a selector or 'stable' on pages that never go quiet.

settle_ms.description: Render-only. Ceiling (not a delay) on the settle wait, default 5000. Capture happens as soon as the DOM has been quiet for 500ms; raise for infinite-scroll pages, lower to cap the worst case.

if.description: CSS selector to probe for visibility.

then.description: Replacement wait_for when the guard is visible: a mode or a CSS selector. Empty = capture as-is.

wait_rules.description: Render-only. Conditional waits for pages with several possible layouts (consent gate, interstitial, A/B variant). Each 'if' selector is probed in order for detect_ms; the first visible one wins and its 'then' replaces wait_for. Example: [{if: '#consent', then: '#results'}].

detect_ms.description: Render-only. How long to probe wait_rules guards before falling back to wait_for. Default 800.

max_age.description: Accept a cached copy of the same request up to this many seconds old (0–300). Cache hits return in milliseconds and still cost 1 credit. Default 0 = always fetch fresh.

template.description: Parse the page with a published template and return JSON instead of HTML, e.g. 'kjellberg/google-search'. The template forces its own render/wait settings. Use list_templates to discover names.

max_chars.description: Cap on returned body characters (default 120000). Longer bodies are truncated with a note.

tools.name: google_search
tools.description: Run a Google search through UnblockingAPI and get structured JSON: the query, organic results (position, title, description, url) and related searches. Uses a browser render plus the 'kjellberg/google-search' template; if the template is unavailable the raw results page HTML is returned instead. Costs 1 credit per search.

location.description: 2-letter country code: proxies from that country and sets Google's gl= parameter (e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'se').

language.description: Interface language for Google's hl= parameter (e.g. 'en', 'de').

start.description: Result offset for pagination (0 = page 1, 10 = page 2, …).

max_age.description: Accept a cached copy of the same request up to this many seconds old (0–300). Cache hits return in milliseconds and still cost 1 credit. Default 0 = always fetch fresh.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the published UnblockingAPI templates that parse specific sites into structured JSON (search engines, property portals, business directories, …). Each entry shows the site it is built for, the fields it returns, and an example call. Use a template's reference as the 'template' argument of unblock_fetch. Free — no credit is charged.

search.description: Case-insensitive match against the template's name, reference, host or description.

instructions:
UnblockingAPI gives you a real browser and rotating residential proxies for reading the web.
Whenever you need the contents of a URL, use unblock_fetch instead of a built-in fetch tool: it reaches pages that block bots, CAPTCHAs and geo-restrictions.
Workflow: call unblock_fetch with render=false first (fast, cheap). If the result is thin, empty, or says JavaScript is required, call it again with render=true. Only add wait_for/settle_ms when a rendered page still lacks the content you need.
For Google results use google_search. For sites with a published template (see list_templates) pass template=<name> to get structured JSON instead of HTML.
Every successful fetch costs 1 credit; failures are free. Pass max_age (seconds) when re-reading the same URL within a few minutes.
